circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island, has been the traditional venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. It represents the second Middle Eastern Grand Prix location to join the F1 calendar, following Bahrain and preceding circuits in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street circuit encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Australian Grand Prix and other racing events under FIA Grade 1 classification. The track serves as the primary venue for Formula One's opening round in the Southern Hemisphere, alongside supporting racing championships and related categories.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally established as the Österreichring and hosted the Austrian Grand Prix continuously from 1970 to 1987. Following a redesign and renaming to the A1-Ring, it resumed hosting the Grand Prix from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street course in Azerbaijan's capital that stretches 6. 003 kilometers, ranking as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One racing. The track hosted the 2016 European Grand Prix as its first top-level motorsport event, followed by the inaugural Azerbaijan Grand Prix in 2017.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix and continues to feature the sport's annual championship race there. The FIA Grade 1-licensed facility accommodates various motorsport categories including GP2 Series, endurance racing, and previously featured Australian V8 Supercars competitions, while offering multiple track configurations for different racing events.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit is renowned for its balanced design combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it a comprehensive test of driver and vehicle capabilities. The track, which holds FIA Grade 1 certification, features grandstands accommodating approximately 140,700 spectators.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Spa-Francorchamps is a 7. 004 km Belgian circuit located near the town of Spa in Wallonia, which has hosted Formula One's Belgian Grand Prix since 1950, the sport's inaugural season. The venue has staged a Grand Prix annually since 1985, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361-kilometer track that serves as the home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the venue has accommodated numerous international racing series including sportscar championships and open-wheel competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading district, this Chinese motorsport facility hosted the Chinese Grand Prix annually between 2004 and 2019, before resuming from 2024 onwards. The venue has expanded its racing calendar to include the Shanghai ePrix since 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Silverstone in Northamptonshire, England, this racing facility has served as the permanent home of the British Grand Prix since 1987, though it previously alternated with other venues between 1955 and 1986. The track gained historic significance by hosting the 1950 British Grand Prix, which marked the inaugural race of the Formula One World Championship. Beyond Formula One, the circuit also stages the British round of motorcycle racing's premier series.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring near Budapest became notable in 1986 as the venue for Formula One's first Grand Prix held within the Eastern Bloc. Built remarkably quickly in just eight months, the 4. 381 km circuit in Mogyoród hosted its inaugural race in March 1986, commemorating Hungarian motorcycle racing pioneer János Drapál.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale di Monza is a 5. 793 km speedway constructed in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built racing circuit. The venue has continuously hosted the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, except for a 1980 closure during renovations, making it one of only four circuits to appear on every Formula One calendar since the championship's inception.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Located in Mie Prefecture, Japan, the Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km figure-eight track operated by Honda Mobilityland that hosts major international motorsport events. The venue, which can accommodate 155,000 spectators, is renowned for staging Formula One World Championship races and serves as a premier destination for top-tier racing competitions.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, following the famous Las Vegas Boulevard where the city's premier hotels and casinos are located. The track incorporates several iconic venues including the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas as it weaves through the urban landscape.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit honoring two Mexican racing brothers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who both perished in racing accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The track has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix on multiple occasions across different eras, with the contemporary iteration beginning in 2015 and now formally branded as the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens that measures 3. 363 miles and incorporates 19 corners, with qualifying lap speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for the Miami Grand Prix, the track joined the Formula One calendar in 2022 and has since become the venue's primary racing use, though Formula E has adapted a modified version of the layout beginning in the 2025-26 season.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a compact 3. 337 km street course that winds through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, encompassing the harbor area of the Principality of Monaco. Though officially known by its full name, the circuit is widely called simply "Monte Carlo" due to its primary location within that neighborhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, the Zandvoort circuit stretches 4. 259 kilometers and hosted the Dutch Grand Prix after returning to Formula One in 2021 following a decades-long absence. The venue's partnership with the sport concluded in 2026, ending its brief tenure on the modern F1 schedule.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a Grade 1 racing facility situated north of Doha in Qatar, spanning 5. 419 kilometers with a prominent 1. 068-kilometer main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, Brazil, Interlagos is a 4. 309 km counterclockwise racing circuit that opened in 1940. The venue was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years earlier, and now serves as his burial site.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: Located along Jeddah's waterfront promenade beside the Red Sea, the Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street-based racing venue that has served as the home of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its inaugural Formula One race in 2021. The track also began hosting international Formula E competition in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Downtown Core and Kallang districts, forming a temporary racing course around the Marina Bay waterfront.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657-kilometre circuit features a balanced design combining extended straightaways with diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing various racing capabilities. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas spans 3. 426 miles and hosts the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside NASCAR and MotoGP events. This FIA Grade 1 facility has also previously accommodated various international racing series including IndyCar, sports car championships, and rallycross competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British racing driver who currently races for Williams in Formula One, competing under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Fernando Alonso is a Spanish driver currently racing for Aston Martin in Formula One, having secured two world championships during his tenure at Renault in 2005 and 2006, along with 32 career Grand Prix victories. Beyond single-seaters, he has achieved significant success in endurance racing, including victories at Le Mans and winning the World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to have claimed titles in both Formula One and world sportscar competition.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli made his Formula One debut in 2025 and has since secured eight race victories. He currently races for Mercedes in the championship.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabriel Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One as part of the Audi racing program, representing his nation in the sport's premier competition.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from his 13 seasons in the sport. He achieved two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship while competing for Mercedes in 2019 and 2020, and has accumulated 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan has competed in seven Formula One races since 2024 while maintaining a reserve role at Haas. Beyond his Formula One commitments, he actively races in the European Le Mans Series' LMP2 category for Nielsen Racing.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly, a French Formula One driver, currently races for Alpine. He achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while driving for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Hadjar, representing France in Formula One, drives for Red Bull Racing and holds dual French and Algerian nationality.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari, having achieved seven World Championship titles matching Michael Schumacher's record. He holds numerous performance records including the most career victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved endurance racing success by winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 competing for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver currently races for Ferrari in Formula One, having secured nine victories throughout his career spanning nine seasons. Leclerc finished as championship runner-up in 2022 while competing for the Scuderia.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: K-Mag is a Danish driver currently competing in endurance racing for BMW's WRT team and part-time in NASCAR's top series. After stints in Formula One between 2014-2020 and 2022-2024, he has shifted his focus to sports car and stock car racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris is a British Formula One driver who secured the 2025 World Drivers' Championship while racing for McLaren. Over his eight seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. Previously competing for Alpine, he secured a Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio "Checo" Pérez, a Mexican driver, currently races for Cadillac in Formula One. The veteran competitor finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while with Red Bull and has claimed six Grand Prix victories during his 15-year career in the sport.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri races for McLaren in Formula One and has claimed nine Grand Prix victories since joining the grid.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his racing career.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell competes for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has claimed eight Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-year career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has secured four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 class for Proton Competition, having previously driven LMP2 machinery in IMSA competition.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian driver currently racing in Formula One for Aston Martin.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Japanese driver Yuki Tsunoda competed in Formula One as a regular competitor between 2021 and 2025 before transitioning to a reserve role for the 2026 season, working with both Red Bull Racing and its sister team Racing Bulls.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Max Verstappen, a Dutch-Belgian driver competing under the Netherlands flag, has claimed four consecutive world titles between 2021 and 2024 while driving for Red Bull Racing. The 72-time Grand Prix winner has established himself as one of Formula One's most successful drivers across his 12-season career.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, China's sole Formula One competitor to date, raced in the sport from 2022 through 2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac. His tenure as an active driver made him a historic figure in the championship's representation of Chinese motorsport talent.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based outfit has competed under the Alpine banner since 2021, serving as Renault's factory team following a rebrand from its previous Renault F1 identity. Operating under various commercial partnerships, the team represented the French manufacturer's motorsport efforts until Renault's withdrawal from the championship at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin is a British automotive manufacturer with a long involvement in Formula One competition, currently fielded under the AMR GP Limited entity as the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of Italian luxury marque Ferrari, stands as Formula One's most enduring and accomplished team, participating in every World Championship season since the sport's inception in 1950. Recognized by their iconic emblem, the team maintains an unparalleled record as both the series' oldest continuously active competitor and its most successful franchise.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas's American-licensed Formula One team debuted in the 2016 season after its establishment in 2014. Following Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024, Ayao Komatsu assumed the role of team principal.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Swiss motorsport engineering firm established in 1970 that progressed from sports car racing, where it secured Le Mans victory in 1989, to Formula One competition beginning in 1993. Operating as an independent constructor for three decades, the outfit became the fourth-longest-tenured team by race entries before being acquired by Audi in 2024 as the foundation for that manufacturer's F1 programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing competes in Formula One as a British outfit headquartered in Woking, operating as a subsidiary within the broader McLaren Group under Bahraini ownership via Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has been a dominant force in Formula One since 1954, operating as both a constructor and engine supplier across multiple eras. The current works team, based in Brackley and racing under the Mercedes-AMG Petronas banner, achieved unprecedented success in recent seasons and underwent ownership restructuring in 2022 when Ineos joined as an equal partner alongside Mercedes-Benz Group and team principal Toto Wolff. The team carries the legendary "Silver Arrows" designation, a historic name associated with German racing excellence.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team that commenced competition in 2024 as one of two constructors under Red Bull GmbH's ownership. Based in Faenza with an additional facility in Milton Keynes, the team operates as Red Bull Racing's sister outfit within the sport's manufacturer network.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that commenced racing in 2024, operating as one of two teams under Red Bull GmbH's ownership alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an additional facility near its sister team in Milton Keynes, the squad represents Red Bull's second constructor entry into the championship.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, competing under an Austrian licence from its English base, emerged as a Formula One outfit in 2005 and has developed into one of two premier-class squads within the Red Bull GmbH portfolio. Christian Horner steered the team's operations for two decades until his 2025 departure, with Laurent Mekies assuming the role of team principal.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's earlier failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in 2026 under the Atlassian Williams F1 Team banner and operates from a substantial 60-acre facility.
